property_summary: mintSynth increases the LP balance of the calling pool, not the member parameter.
After mintSynth, the LP balance of the calling pool must increase.

For any pool caller, the LP balance credited in mapSynth_LPBalance is always associated with msg.sender (the pool) and never with the member receiving synthetic tokens; the buggy version credits the LP balance to the member instead, causing a discrepancy that can be observed by checking mapSynth_LPBalance after a mintSynth call.

In the correct contract, mapSynth_LPBalance tracks LP units by the pool caller (msg.sender), whereas the buggy version credits them to the member, so for any pool calling mintSynth, the credited LP balance moves to the member instead of the pool.
After mintSynth is called, mapSynth_LPBalance[pool] should increase by the added LP units, but the buggy version leaves it unchanged, increasing mapSynth_LPBalance[member] instead.

For any pool caller, after calling mintSynth, the sum of mapSynth_LPBalance over all keys must equal the sum of mapSynth_LPDebt over all keys; the buggy version credits LP balance to member instead of pool, breaking this invariant when the same pool mints for different members.

For any pool and member, after mintSynth(member, amount) is called by that pool, the sum of mapSynth_LPBalance over the pool and the member must equal the sum of mapSynth_LPDebt over the same keys minus the minted amount, which holds in the reference but the buggy version breaks it by crediting LP balance to the member instead of the pool.
Increasing LP units in mintSynth by the minted amount instead of actual LP units causes the LP balance to exceed the LP debt after a single mint and no other operations.

property_summary: In mintSynth, the increase in LP balance (mapSynth_LPBalance[pool]) should equal the increase in LP tokens held by the contract (pool token balance of address(this)), not the amount of synth minted.
In mintSynth, the increase in mapSynth_LPBalance[pool] must equal the difference between the pool token balance of this contract before and after the call, which is the actual LP units added.
After a successful mintSynth call, the LP balance mapped for the caller pool must not exceed the LP debt mapped for that pool.
After mintSynth succeeds, the increase in the pool's mapped LP balance equals the increase in the pool token balance of the contract.
